pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: test/done.test.js AC-1 checks existing rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2; migration 0002 adds the column with default 0.
test/done.test.js AC-2 checks / and ?view=open list only open items in id order.
AC-3 test: done view lists ✓-marked items in id order, with ids marked out of order (3, 1).
AC-4 test: all view lists every item in id order, with ✓ only on done ones.
AC-5 test compares exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is a <strong>, not a link.
AC-6 test: Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values all answer 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.

The last commit (1e18841) reworded AC-7 to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step, and removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title. No test names AC-7 now. The behaviour does work, and the unnamed test and the state tests cover it, but under the rules the item is unmet.
AC-8 test asserts traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all.

findings.what: A late commit (1e18841, 'Follow-up edits') changed AC-7 to 'verified by review: checked by hand' and renamed its test so it no longer names AC-7. This came after the owner's go of 2026-10-12, and the spec records no owner decision for it. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable step. The result is an acceptance item with no named test and no real review step.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit and restore the 'AC-7:' prefix in the test title. If the owner really wants it verified by review, record that as a dated decision and give a concrete step.

findings.what: The AC-7 test lost its AC-7 name, so no test is tied to the item. The same commit removed the link between the spec and its proof.
The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and 'covers AC-1 to AC-8'. Both are false: the final commit edited the AC-7 text after the go, and the AC-7 test is no longer named.
findings.fix: Correct the PR text, or revert the edit so the claims hold.

findings.what: The README doesn't say that other view values answer 400. It also doesn't say that traffic routes may now carry a query string.
findings.fix: Add a short note on both.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The late edit to AC-7 is the problem; the rest follows the spec and its decisions.
The AC-7 edit came after the go with no recorded owner decision. All other items are met. Every state-table row has a test.

I did not run the tests, because the workers test runtime was not run here. By reading, the tests assert behaviour. The AC-7 test lost its name. The traffic test helper was widened to track the query string, which is not a loosening.
The README is updated for the views. The 400 behaviour is not mentioned.
The view is validated with Object.hasOwn and the SQL fragments are constants, so there is no injection. The empty-table logic is correct.
The view value is checked against an allow-list. Titles are HTML-escaped. No secrets, and no instructions planted in the repository.
The diff has a UI: server-rendered HTML in src/index.js. The design lens is skipped for lack of a browser; the markup is a plain nav and list.
No browser was available. The rendered HTML is asserted in tests.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, given the AC-7 edit in commit 1e18841.
